summary.tldr: Creates rules to reduce federal barriers to interprovincial trade and labour mobility, and sets a special process for certain projects named in the national interest.
what_it_does: Creates a federal framework that treats goods and services meeting provincial or territorial requirements as meeting comparable federal requirements for interprovincial movement.
Recognizes provincial and territorial occupational authorizations, and can issue comparable federal authorizations to people who hold them.
Lets the Governor in Council make regulations about federal barriers to moving goods, services, and labour within Canada.
Lets the Governor in Council add a project and a short description to a schedule if it is considered to be in the national interest.
Deems certain findings and opinions under other federal laws to have been made in favour of projects named in Schedule 1, for the authorizations needed to carry them out.

Requires a designated minister to issue a document setting out project conditions, and that document is treated as the required authorizations named in it. It also requires an annual independent review of each national interest project.
summary.background: The bill was introduced in the House of Commons on 6 June 2025 and had first reading that day. It would enact the Free Trade and Labour Mobility in Canada Act and the Building Canada Act.
